blocks.label: Populism, populist ideology and liberalism
blocks.description: Thirteen dimensions scored on 0–10 by three model families from the full manifesto text, each with a verbatim evidence quote. Scores are aggregated as in Rode & Stöckl (2026): a chunk counts if the model marks its evidence as verified and the quote is found verbatim in the manifesto chunk (and is not copied from the prompt); confidence-weighted mean within model, plain mean across models.
headline: populism_overall
liberalism_overall
pop_ideology_direction

dims.label: Populism (overall)
dims.description: Rounded mean of the three populism sub-dimensions, adjusted by one point for breadth.

dims.label: Anti-elitism
dims.description: Elites or the establishment framed as corrupt or out of touch.

dims.label: People-centrism
dims.description: 'The people' invoked as a unified, virtuous group.

dims.label: Populist ideology (strength)
dims.description: Overall strength of the populist ideological flavour (not its direction).

dims.label: Ideology: centrist
dims.description: Generic people–elite appeals without a clear programmatic stance.

dims.label: Liberalism (overall)
dims.description: Rounded mean of the four liberalism sub-dimensions with evidence.

dims.label: Political liberalism
dims.description: Democracy, rule of law, checks and balances, media freedom, due process.

dims.label: Social liberalism
dims.description: Civil rights, minority protection, gender and LGBTQ+ equality, pluralism.

dims.label: Economic liberalism
dims.description: Free markets, competition, enterprise, deregulation, tax efficiency, trade openness.

dims.label: Financial-market liberalism
dims.description: Market pricing of assets and credit, open banking and capital markets, enabling prudential rules.

derived.label: Ideology direction (right − left)
derived.description: (R − L) / (R + L + C) on the cross-model means of the right, left and centrist scores; −1 left, +1 right.
